title: BrandDealQuote
description: The native product contract. Downstream consumers read this object; nothing is parsed back out of the Creator-facing text. Three shapes here exist to stop a familiar failure: sources that disagree are carried side by side instead of averaged, a price is never emitted while the terms that decide it are still open, and every figure names the evidence class it came from.

currency.description: This version prices in USD only. A local-currency band would need local benchmarks, and converting a US band at today's rate would dress a US number up as a local one.

stale.description: True once the framework is older than its staleness budget. Rates move; a stale table still describes the levers correctly but its numbers stop being current.

determinacy.description: terms_incomplete whenever usage rights or exclusivity are unspecified. It is the normal state of an opening brief, and it forbids a headline number rather than degrading one.

usage_rights_grant.description: Whether the brief licenses the content at all. none is a settled term - no reuse, no paid use, no buyout - and carries no usage-rights lever; it is never priced as a short licence.

package_totals.description: One total per benchmark source. There is deliberately no combined figure: two sources that disagree by 10x do not have a meaningful midpoint.

transacted_reference.description: What money actually changed hands for comparable work, where such a source exists. It answers a question the rate tables cannot: how far published asking ranges sit from settled amounts.

caveat.description: Travels with the number, because an average across all tiers compared against one tier's band is a false comparison.

reach_estimate.description: A second pricing route, from delivered views rather than follower count. Present only when it can be computed and only when it disagrees with the follower-tier route by more than the framework's threshold, because agreement between the two carries no information the creator needs.

brand_ad_context.description: Present only when an advertising-activity lookup ran. It sits outside every priced structure on purpose: it changes how the creator talks to this brand, never what the work is worth.

open_terms.description: Terms the brief left unsettled, each with what it costs to leave open and the question that settles it. In review mode this is the deliverable, not a footnote.

price_impact.description: unpriced means no source prices this term; it still has to be settled in writing.

should_state_a_number.description: False whenever determinacy is terms_incomplete. Naming a figure first anchors the deal, and the unsettled terms are most of the price.

opening_ask.description: Only ever populated when the terms are settled. Carries the opening premium over the target, so the creator has somewhere to move.

data_gaps.description: Account figures that could not be obtained, and what each one would have decided. A gap is 'could not tell', never 'does not apply'.

code.description: Stable identifier for the gap, so the Creator-facing layer can say it in the reader's language instead of restating the English.

legal_review.const: This prices a scope. It is not a legal review of the contract, and it does not approve any term.
legal_review.description: Fixed text, because a pricing tool that drifts into approving terms is the failure this boundary exists to prevent.

not_a_platform_payout.const: Sponsorship fees and platform payouts have different units and different evidence. Nothing here estimates platform ad revenue.

brand_budget_not_inferred.const: Nothing here estimates what the brand can afford. Observable advertising activity is not a budget.

income_rows.description: The brand-deal part of an income breakdown: one row per deliverable per published reading. A second reading of the same line is marked as already inside the first, never added to it; while the price-deciding terms are open a row carries no amount. See income-row.v1.schema.json.

income_totals.description: Sums over rows sharing one rate origin, period and currency. Empty by default.

income_breakdown_requested.description: True when the request asked for an income breakdown; the report then prints the rows as a table.

sources.description: Every public source this quote cites, with the page a reader can check it against. Observed listings and the internal framework have no public page and are not listed.

base_bands.description: Every benchmark band whose follower range contains this account, one entry per source. Sources draw their tier boundaries differently, so the same account can be mid-tier in one and micro in another; both are shown.

adjusted_bands.description: Base band with the levers applied, still one entry per source and still never merged.

line_totals.description: Each adjusted band times the line's quantity, one entry per source. A package total is the sum of these, so the lines the report prints add up to it.

unpriced_terms.description: Terms that apply to this line but that no source prices. They are listed, not silently valued at zero.

sample_size.description: How many listings the band was computed from, for an observed band. A compiled band has none, because the compilation does not publish its sample.

applied_lever.$comment: 'platform' is deliberately absent from the kind enum. Platform differences already sit inside the per-platform base bands; re-applying them as a lever would charge for the same difference twice.

price_impact.description: Fixed, and checked. Advertising spend and creator budget are different lines in a brand's plan; a heavy advertiser can hold a small creator budget and often does. The moment this evidence is allowed to move a number, the Skill is inferring a budget it cannot see.

posture.description: What the reading amounts to for the conversation. A name that did not match is its own outcome, not a quiet advertiser: collapsing the two would turn a spelling difference into a claim about the brand.

posture_note.description: What this changes about the conversation rather than the price.

caveats.description: The first two always travel: coverage is one ecosystem, and ad activity is not a creator budget.

divergence_ratio.description: How far this route sits from the follower-tier route, as a ratio of midpoints, always at least 1.

interpretation.description: Which way the disagreement runs, which is the part that changes what the creator should do.
